issues.legal_issue: Possession that is prima facie lawful gives rise to a rebuttable presumption of ownership against the government, which must prove its subsisting title to displace that presumption.
A government cannot dispossess persons in lawful possession of land for a public purpose without following authority of law and the applicable process for acquisition or resumption.
A condition barring compensation when assigned land is resumed for a public purpose is unconstitutional, and assignees are entitled to compensation equivalent to the land’s full market value.

Courts deciding title suits against the government must account for the government’s presumptive claim to unoccupied land and scrutinize the claimant’s documentary title, revenue records, and nature and duration of possession.

A notice under Section 80 of the Code of Civil Procedure must give the government an opportunity to assess and potentially settle the claim, and public authorities are expected to communicate their position rather than remain unresponsive.
